name: Jehu
overview: Jehu was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, known specifically as the Anathothite. He is noted for having come to King David at Ziklag, indicating his allegiance and support during David's reign. His identification as the Anathothite highlights his geographical and tribal roots within Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehu means 'y-h-v-h is he,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the LORD. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:3, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries a significant meaning tied to the divine name of God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jehu as a descendant of Benjamin, confirming his tribal lineage. No additional family relationships are mentioned beyond this tribal affiliation and his unique designation as the Anathothite.
scriptureSignificance: Jehu's significance lies in his loyalty to King David, as demonstrated by his coming to David at Ziklag. His tribal identity as a Benjaminite and connection to Anathoth situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's consolidation under David's kingship. This highlights the unity among the tribes and the support David received from diverse regions and clans.
